assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Use periodicity to reduce an arbitrary real x to its fractional part t in [0,1). Let m = floor(n*t). The floor characterization places t in the interval [m/n,(m+1)/n), and on that interval the expression is bounded above by the discrete surrogate g_n(m). The finite bottleneck lemma shows g_n(m) <= H_n - 1 for all m, so f_n(x) <= H_n - 1 for every x. On the other hand, if t is in the top interval [1 - 1/n,1), then every floor(k*t) equals k - 1, so f_n(t) = H_n - 1. The strict part of the discrete bottleneck excludes all other intervals. Therefore the maximum is H_n - 1, achieved exactly when the fractional part of x lies in [1 - 1/n,1).

payload.theorem_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: First reduce an arbitrary real x to its fractional part t = x - floor(x). By integer-shift invariance, f_n(x) = f_n(t), and the standard fractional-part identity gives 0 <= t < 1. For such a t, let m = floor(n*t). The floor-interval lemma places t in [m/n, (m+1)/n), and the interval comparison gives f_n(t) <= g_n(m). The discrete bottleneck lemma then yields g_n(m) <= H_n - 1, so every reduced t in [0,1) satisfies f_n(t) <= H_n - 1, hence every real x satisfies f_n(x) <= H_n - 1. On the top interval [1 - 1/n, 1), the explicit computation shows floor(k*t) = k - 1 for all 1 <= k <= n, so f_n(t) = H_n - 1; by periodicity this gives equality for every x whose fractional part lies in that interval. If the fractional part t is smaller than 1 - 1/n, then m = floor(n*t) cannot equal n - 1, so the equality case in the discrete lemma is impossible; this forces strict inequality f_n(x) < H_n - 1. Therefore the global maximizers are exactly the real numbers x whose fractional part x - floor(x) lies in [1 - 1/n, 1), equivalently x = z + t with z an integer and t in [1 - 1/n, 1), and the maximal value is H_n - 1.
